claim.claim-text: 1. A method, comprising: at an electronic device (1900) with a display (1938), one or more processors, and memory:

while displaying the first user interface, detecting an input; and in accordance with a determination that the input corresponds to the first complication, launching a heart-rate monitoring application.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein displaying the first user interface further includes a second complication (1934) different from the first complication, wherein the second complication is an affordance for launching a workout application different from the heart-rate monitoring application.

3. The method of claim 2, further comprising: in accordance with a determination that the input corresponds to the second complication, launching a workout application different from the heart-rate monitoring application.
4. The method of any preceding claim, wherein displaying the first user interface further includes: while displaying the first user interface:
receiving data corresponding to a heart rate of the user; and displaying, within the second complication, a graphical representation corresponding to the heart rate of the user.
5. The method of claim 4, wherein displaying the graphical representation includes displaying an animation of a pulsing heart.

6. The method of any preceding claim, wherein displaying the first user interface further includes a first visual indication of a physical activity of the user and a second visual indication of a physical activity of the user, wherein the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user and the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user are different.

7. The method of claim 6, wherein the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user corresponds to the physical activity of the user over a first time range, and the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user corresponds to the physical activity of the user over a second time range, wherein the first time range and the second time range are different.
8. The method of claim 6 or 7, further comprising:

detecting a change in the physical activity of the user; and in response to detecting the change in the physical activity of the user, updating the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user.

9. The method of any of claims 6-8, wherein the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user and the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user are concentric rings.

10. The method of any of claims 6-9, wherein the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user and the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user are non-concentric rings.

11. The method of any of claims 6-10, wherein displaying the first user interface further includes a clock hand that overlaps the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user, and does not overlap the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user.

12. The method of any of claims 6-11, wherein displaying the first user interface further includes a clock hand that overlaps the first visual indication of the physical activity of the user and the second visual indication of the physical activity of the user.

13. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the clock face includes a first clock hand, a second clock hand, and a third clock hand, preferably wherein the first, second and third hands are an hour hand, a minute hand and seconds hand respectively.

14. A computer-readable medium comprising one or more programs configured to be executed by one or more processors of an electronic device with a display, the one or more programs including instructions for performing the method of any preceding claim.
